title: 1 cm ruler with 12 divisions sells 3 papers: Central South University reports academic misconduct, confirmed
excerpt: The Xiangya-affiliated papers that netizens dug up—where a "1-centimeter scale actually had 12 tick marks on it"—have now received an official conclusion. Centr
content_html:
The Xiangya-affiliated papers that netizens dug up—where a "1-centimeter scale actually had 12 tick marks on it"—have now received an official conclusion. Central South University announced today that, in response to online doubts about three papers from Xiangya Second Hospital and Xiangya Hospital, the university organized peer experts to check experimental records, raw data, and submission records. After review by the university's Academic Style Construction Committee, all three papers were confirmed to involve academic misconduct.

Three papers, three diseases

The named papers span three journals: a 2025 Journal of Translational Medicine nasopharyngeal carcinoma study (first author Deng [name withheld], corresponding author Zhao [name withheld]) was found to have fabricated and falsified data and figures, along with improper authorship and violations of research ethics; a 2026 Cell Death & Disease cancer study (first author Cai [name withheld], co-first author Tan [name withheld], corresponding author Zhao [name withheld]) was found to have fabrication and falsification plus improper authorship; and a 2026 Scientific Reports paper (corresponding author Deng [name withheld]) also involved fabrication and falsification. Netizens became suspicious after noticing unusual flaws in the experimental images and suspected the images were AI-generated; the topic once trended on Weibo's hot search list.

The penalties were not light: Deng and Zhao were demoted in professional and technical post rank, lost eligibility for professional title promotion, talent program applications, graduate student admissions, and awards and honors for 5 years, and were barred from undertaking science and technology activities supported by government funds for 10 years; Cai and Tan likewise had the above qualifications frozen for 5 years and were barred from government-funded science and technology projects for 5 years; the remaining authors received academic admonishment talks. The university stated it has "zero tolerance" for academic misconduct. The Hunan Provincial Department of Science and Technology had already instructed Xiangya Second Hospital to investigate on November 17—from hot search to substantiation, only two days passed.
